 Author Cassidy Wong Created On 2026-11-06 Edited On 2026-11-06 Text Size A A A Japan implemented a new "pay first, refund later" tax system for travelers starting November 1, 2026: eligible travelers must pay the tax-inclusive price when shopping at duty-free shops and complete customs confirmation within 90 days of departure. The corresponding consumption tax will then be refunded by the shop or its authorized service provider. Kwiksure has compiled information on Japan's new tax refund system, detailing the refund process and eligibility requirements, and comparing various tax refund platforms and methods.

 Key Summary
 Tax refund threshold: The total amount of eligible goods purchased from the same store on the same day must reach 5,000 yen before tax.
 Airport procedure: Complete customs confirmation before checking in your baggage and prepare to present your goods as required.
 Product regulations: The classification of general goods and consumables has been removed; the 500,000 yen limit on consumables and the requirement for special packaging have been eliminated.
 Online processing: Seven designated airports support online confirmation via Visit Japan Web and dedicated Wi-Fi.
 Refund arrangements: The method and procedure will be as instructed by the store, and refunds will not be processed by customs.
 What is Japan's new tax refund system? How does it differ from the old system?
 Japan's new tax refund system has changed from the old instant tax refund to a system where customers pay first and then receive a refund. Travelers must pay the tax-inclusive price when shopping, and the consumption tax will be refunded by the store through the tax refund platform only after customs confirms the goods have left the country at the airport or port. 
 New tax refund system
(Effective November 1, 2026) 
 Old tax refund system
(Until October 31, 2026) 
 Tax refund methods 
 Settle the bill at the price including tax. Before departing, complete customs confirmation procedures at the airport or port before checking in your luggage, and then receive the tax refund through the tax refund platform. 
 Present your passport and pay the tax-free price immediately, or pay the price including tax first and then process the tax refund at the designated counter on the same day. 
 Product Categories 
 Cancel product category 
 "General goods" and "consumables" are calculated separately. If they are refunded together, they will be treated as consumables. 
 Tax refund threshold 
 Tax refunds are available for purchases of 5,000 yen or more before tax. 
 Tax refunds are available for purchases of 5,000 yen or more before tax. 
 Consumption cap 
 No daily or single-store spending limit 
 Consumables daily limit of 500,000 yen per store 
 Packaging regulations 
 No specific requirements for sealed packaging 
 Consumables must be sealed in packaging and must not be opened before leaving the country. 
 High consumption 
 Purchases exceeding 1 million yen will be assigned a unique serial number for easy tracking. 
 For purchases exceeding 1 million yen, the store must retain a copy of your passport. 
 Customs confirmation 
 Before checking in your luggage, use the airport's dedicated Wi-Fi to visit the Japan website or complete customs clearance at the self-service kiosks. 
 Goods are usually not required to be presented to customs upon departure; customs only conducts random checks. 
 Tax refund arrangements 
 The method and procedure are as instructed by the store; tax refunds are not processed by customs. 
 Tax refunds can be processed directly in the store or at a designated counter on the same day. 
 Exit restrictions 
 The item must undergo customs inspection within 90 days of purchase. 
 Goods are generally allowed to leave the country within 180 days, and consumables within 30 days. 
 What are the eligibility requirements, eligibility criteria, and product restrictions for tax refunds in Japan?
 The new system eliminates the distinction between general goods and consumables, and also removes the 500,000 yen tax-free cap on consumables; however, travelers must still meet the minimum spending threshold and departure time requirements.
 Which travelers are eligible for tax refunds?
 Foreign travelers who have been in Japan for a short period of less than 6 months
 Japanese citizens residing overseas who have temporarily returned to Japan for less than 6 months
 Purchases totaling 5,000 yen (excluding tax) at the same store on the same day
 Travelers need to make purchases of 5,000 yen (excluding tax) at the same store on the same day to meet the tax-free threshold.
 What are the regulations regarding duty-free goods in Japan?
 The new tax refund system will eliminate categorization. Consumables do not need to be sealed in special packaging bags; travelers can purchase daily necessities, snacks, and electrical appliances together. No upper limit on the amount of tax refunds. You can get a tax refund at the airport as long as you meet the store's minimum tax-free threshold and present your receipt. However, duty-free consumables still cannot be used in Japan and must be taken out of the country by the traveler in person. 
 Which goods are ineligible for tax refunds?
 Gold, gold bars, gold coins, platinum coins, etc.
 Gift certificates, vouchers
 Service consumption and non-physical goods such as restaurant dining fees, theme park tickets, transportation tickets, and hotel accommodation fees.
 Items already consumed domestically or not taken out of the country; if the consumables have been consumed or opened in Japan, or if the goods were not presented to customs upon departure, the eligibility for a tax refund for the entire purchase will be cancelled.
 Tax refund processing time: Customs confirmation upon departure must be completed within 90 days of purchase.
 Passengers must complete departure customs confirmation within 90 days of purchasing duty-free goods. If they fail to do so within the time limit or violate relevant regulations, their eligibility for a tax refund will be directly cancelled.
 Japan Tax Refund Process: Shopping, Departure Confirmation, and Refund
 1. Confirm that the store is a qualified duty-free shop.
 Before purchasing duty-free goods, you should first check whether the store displays the "Japan. Tax-Free Shop" label. Only stores with this label are eligible for tax refunds.
 2. Present your passport and pay the price including tax at checkout.
 Shop at the same store on the same day, up to the tax-free threshold, present your original passport or the tax-free QR code on the Visit Japan Web to register your purchase, and pay the price including tax.
 3. Register tax exemption information and obtain a tax refund list.
 Merchants will provide a QR code or registration information specifically for tax refunds. Travelers can scan the code with their mobile phones to access the official tax refund platform (such as J-TaxRefund ), register an account, verify their passport, and specify their refund method. Since registration requires linking a credit card and verification, it is recommended to complete the registration process after returning to the hotel.
 4. Complete customs confirmation before shipment.
 After arriving at the airport, passengers need to connect to the dedicated tax refund Wi-Fi in the international departure hall, then open Visit Japan Web to complete the customs confirmation process, or go directly to the tax-free self-service kiosk.
 When the customs inspection shows a green "Completed" message, it means that customs has confirmed the completion of the inspection; if it shows a red "Not Complete" message, you must go to the customs counter for manual inspection; if a black cross appears, it means that after customs confirmation, it is determined that you do not possess the relevant items, or that the 90-day period has expired, and you do not meet the requirements for a tax refund. Passengers should complete the tax refund confirmation before checking in their luggage, as customs may need to inspect duty-free goods. 
 5. Follow the store's instructions to complete the refund process and check the progress.
 After receiving the customs approval notice, the duty-free platform selected by the store will usually refund the tax to the credit card previously registered by the traveler within 2 to 4 weeks. Travelers can check the progress on the platform's official website or app. If you choose a cash refund, you need to go to the "cash refund machine" to collect Japanese yen cash after obtaining customs' departure confirmation.
 How do I complete departure customs confirmation using Visit Japan Web?
 Is Visit Japan Web mandatory?
 Visit Japan Web is not the only way to complete departure customs confirmation; travelers can also queue at the self-service kiosks on-site. If passengers wish to process their requests online, they must log in to Visit Japan Web using the airport's dedicated Wi-Fi. 
 How do I register and connect to the airport's dedicated Wi-Fi?
 Upon arrival at the airport's international departure hall (before baggage check-in and security check), connect to the dedicated Wi-Fi.
 Login information for the dedicated network (subject to on-site announcements from customs or the airport)
 Network Name (SSID): Customs_WiFi_For_TaxRefund
Password: jcustoms
 Open Visit Japan Web , click "Tax Refund Procedures".
 Verify the tax-free purchase records displayed in the system within the past 90 days and click Confirm.
 A green light indicates that customs confirmation is complete; if a red light is displayed, you must proceed to the on-site customs counter for inspection.
 How do I register my passport and entry permit information?
 Entry into Japan requires registration in advance on Visit Japan Web . To create a duty-free shopping QR code in Visit Japan Web for online customs confirmation upon departure, you must first log in to your entry permit stamp information.
 Log in to Visit Japan Web . Under "Use after entering Japan", select "Procedures for Tax-free shopping and tax refund".
 Log in with your passport's facial image and landing permission seal details. Once completed, it will display "Registered".
 Before departure, connect to the dedicated network and click the "Tax Refund Procedure" button to open a separate page for Customs confirmation procedures

 How do I receive my Japanese tax refund? How long does it take for it to arrive in my account?
 Under Japan's new tax refund system, tax refunds are no longer processed by airport customs; customs is only responsible for verifying the physical goods being shipped out of the country. Japanese businesses typically entrust specific tax refund platforms to process the refunds. The specific details regarding refund methods, processing times, and handling fees vary depending on the store and tax refund platform. Travelers need to register and confirm with the duty-free shop where they made the purchase or its partner tax refund platform.

 What should I do if I haven't received my refund after customs confirmation?
 Under Japan's new tax refund system, customs is only responsible for verifying the physical goods being shipped out of the country. The tax-free platform will only refund the tax according to the method chosen by the tourist after receiving notification of approval from customs; therefore, refunds cannot be received immediately. Travelers can use the channels provided by the tax refund platform to check the current refund progress and confirm the accuracy of their refund account or credit card information. If the refund has not been processed within the normal processing time, or if the refund status shows "failed," they need to contact the tax refund platform's customer service for further inquiry.

 Common Mistakes Regarding Tax Refunds in Japan
 1. Forgot to present passport or failed to register tax exemption information
 If a tax refund is required, the traveler must notify the cashier at checkout so that the cashier can scan the traveler's passport and upload the transaction information to the Japan National Tax Agency's cloud system in real time. If tourists pay the standard price including tax and do not register for tax exemption, the customs system will not have this record, and a tax refund will not be possible. 
 2. Duty-free goods already checked in before departure
 Airport self-service tax refund machines randomly check passports during scanning. If a red light appears, it means the passenger needs to proceed to the customs counter for manual inspection with all duty-free goods. If the goods have already been checked in as baggage, customs will refuse to process the refund. Customs confirmation must be completed before baggage is checked in. 
 3. Leaving the country more than 90 days after purchase.
 Japan's tax-free law strictly stipulates that foreign tourists must take duty-free goods purchased in Japan out of the country within 90 days of the purchase date. If more than 90 days have passed, the system will automatically determine that the tourist has left the goods in Japan for use, and the tax refund for that transaction will be automatically cancelled.
 4. Duty-free consumables opened or used within Japan
 Although under the new system, duty-free consumables do not need to be sealed in special packaging bags, they still cannot be used in Japan and must be taken out of the country by the traveler in person. Otherwise, all goods in the record will not be confirmed, and no tax refund will be possible.
 5. Lost duty-free shopping receipt
 Since many tax refund platforms require customers to scan the tax-free QR code on the receipt before registering their credit card for a refund, if the receipt is lost before registration, customs will be unable to process the transaction and therefore cannot issue a tax refund. However, if the shop assistant has already uploaded the traveler's information and passport at the duty-free shop, the transaction will still be recorded upon departure, even if the receipt is lost. Nevertheless, regardless of whether tourists need to register their purchases themselves, they should still keep all duty-free receipts safe or take photos of them with their phones for future reference.
 Preparatory work for the trip to Japan
 1. Credit card theft/cash theft loss protection
 Shopping sprees in Japan come with risks of loss, theft, or misuse, regardless of whether you pay by credit card or cash. When buying travel insurance , pay special attention to whether different plans include coverage for credit card fraud and cash theft losses, making your trip more worry-free.
 2. Personal property protection
 Many people buy high-priced items during their travels, so it is very important to compare travel insurance plans. When choosing a travel insurance plan, you can also check the total compensation limit for personal property protection, as well as the individual compensation limits for items such as mobile phones, laptops, and cameras, to assess whether the compensation amount is sufficient.

 Frequently Asked Questions
 Can duty-free consumables be used in Japan?
 No. If the duty-free consumables have been opened before departure, they are considered to have been used within Japan, and if discovered, the entire purchase will be eligible for a tax refund.
 Can I use Visit Japan Web instead of the self-service tax refund machine?
 Yes. At the seven major airports of Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu, New Chitose, Fukuoka, and Naha, you can use the airport's dedicated Wi-Fi to log in to Visit Japan Web to complete customs confirmation.
 How long does it take to confirm receipt of a tax refund at the airport kiosk?
 Regardless of waiting time, the self-service tax refund machine only takes a few seconds to read your passport and display the result. However, if the machine displays a red result, you will need to go to the customs counter for inspection, which takes longer.
 Are there any processing fees for tax refunds in Japan?
 It depends on the regulations of the store and the tax refund platform. Usually, both the store and the tax refund platform will state the tax refund processing fee they charge. Some shops also hold special events where the handling fee will be directly refunded at a discount.
